sections.title: /  Technologies We Use for Business Process Automation

items.q: What is the difference between BPA and RPA?
items.a: Business Process Automation (BPA) focuses on automating complete workflows across systems and departments. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is usually used for repetitive rule-based tasks such as data entry or document processing. Modern BPA solutions often combine automation workflows, integrations, and AI-assisted operations.

items.q: What processes should be automated first in a business?
items.a:
The best starting point is usually repetitive workflows that create delays, manual overhead, or operational bottlenecks. Common examples include approvals, reporting, onboarding, customer support workflows, CRM updates, and invoice processing. AI-assisted automation is especially useful for data-heavy and repetitive operational tasks.
As part of this process, the client receives a helicopter view of their current process landscape - a clear, structured picture of where the gaps, inefficiencies, and automation opportunities actually live across the business. This birds-eye perspective allows leadership to prioritize automation initiatives not in isolation, but in the context of the full operational map, ensuring the highest-impact processes are addressed first.

items.q: How can automation reduce costs and improve ROI for my business?
items.a: Business automation services help reduce manual work, improve operational efficiency, minimize errors, and accelerate everyday workflows. AI-powered automation also improves visibility and supports faster operational decision-making across teams.

items.q: Can business process automation integrate with existing systems?
items.a: Yes. Automation systems can integrate with CRMs, ERP platforms, databases, internal tools, and operational software without rebuilding existing infrastructure. A reliable process automation company can also connect AI-assisted workflows across disconnected systems and improve how operational data is processed and organized.

items.q: Is business process automation scalable as a business grows?
items.a: Yes. Scalable automation systems support growing workloads, larger teams, and more complex operational workflows. AI-assisted automation helps businesses maintain efficiency, visibility, and process consistency as operations expand.

items.q: How long does it take to implement business process automation?
items.a: Implementation timelines depend on the complexity of the workflows, the number of systems involved, and the level of customization required. Smaller automation projects can often be launched within a few weeks, while larger operational transformations may require phased implementation. Most companies start with one high-impact workflow and expand automation gradually across departments.

items.q: Will automation replace employees or change internal roles?
items.a: Business process automation is typically used to reduce repetitive manual work rather than replace teams. Automation helps employees spend less time on operational tasks like data transfer, approvals, reporting, or document handling, allowing them to focus on strategic, creative, or customer-facing responsibilities. In many cases, automation also improves collaboration and reduces operational stress across teams.

items.q: How do companies measure the success of automation projects?
items.a: Automation success is usually measured through operational improvements such as reduced processing time, fewer manual errors, faster response times, improved visibility, and lower operational costs. Many businesses also track employee productivity, workflow consistency, customer experience improvements, and scalability as automation adoption grows across the organization.

items.q: 9: Does your process automation comply with the EU AI Act?
items.a:
Yes. As AI systems face increasing regulatory oversight, compliance is a core part of how AltheraCode designs and delivers automation solutions.
Before any automation is built, AltheraCode assesses whether AI components within a workflow fall under high-risk, limited-risk, or minimal-risk categories as defined by the EU AI Act. This helps determine the appropriate system architecture, documentation requirements, and governance controls.
To support transparency and regulatory compliance, AI-powered workflows can include audit trails, logging, and decision tracking, helping organizations maintain visibility into how automated processes operate and make decisions.
